text: On the bus back to Seoul, Taeo couldn't forget Grandpa's warning. The man who said everything was fine had told him never to enter a gate.
Nib asked what Grandpa had said at the bus door. Taeo dismissed it as nothing. Nib had heard it himself, but let the answer stand.
Twenty days remained until the review. Nib kept scouting at Minho's yard, warning the crew about hazards such as a bent screen foot. Taeo became very good at watching.
The receipts accumulated in their folder. Nib put his earnings in a biscuit tin and kept working toward the hearing.
Eunchae taught him Hangul in the break room. He practised reading his name, then proudly sounded out cross-contamination. That card belonged to Eunchae's food licence exam pile.

Meanwhile, the construct took Taeo's night shifts. He got weekends. Watching it stand motionless after work, Nib asked who took over from it. Nobody did; constructs didn't tire. Nib observed that nobody came for it.
The night before the review, Taeo wrote everything he intended to say for Nib. Nib watched him and pointed out that the panel would be asking him.
They reached the agency the next morning. Eunchae was covering Taeo's shift. Her message told him to stop apologising and reminded Nib not to rush his vowels.
Security took Nib's knife until they left. He reluctantly surrendered it, warning the guard not to drop it. It was a good knife.
Upstairs, Pyo handed a coffee to Chae's supervisor with the ease of an old acquaintance. Nib walked past his warm greeting.
The supervisor privately urged Chae to withdraw her arrival report and let Kanghan classify Nib. She refused. Nib wasn't theirs. If she had to defend the report, her name was already on it.
Inside the hearing room, Nib counted one door. Taeo had counted too. The chair opened proceedings: Kanghan wanted Nib's pending arrival status changed to construct. She referred to him as 'it.'
Pyo presented his argument. Advanced constructs could imitate speech and learn which words moved people without understanding them. Nib reached instinctively for his knife and found the empty sheath.
Chae cited the arrival category in the 1995 Act, unused for twenty years. When shown a form offering only hunter or construct, Nib had told her he wasn't a box.

Minho produced receipts for nine jobs, twenty thousand won each, paid directly to Nib. Challenged that payment proved little, he added that Nib had refused a tenth job for a Hangul lesson. Minho had seen him choose.
Bae hurried in late, leaving his golem outside the door. He testified that Nib had saved his delivery. Paying 640,000 won a month for a construct, he knew what one was. Nib wasn't one.
The chair asked Taeo what Nib was. Taeo folded away his prepared notes. Instead of answering for him, he said, 'You should ask Nib.'
The lectern hid almost all of Nib. Asked to stand where they could see him, he stepped into the open floor.
He chose a position facing the door and admitted he was afraid of rooms with only one exit. The chair stopped writing and asked what he was.
Nib answered that he was a scout. He kept watch at a wall above the lower path. Kett had been coming to take over his watch.
Now Kett would find the post empty and go looking for him. Nib's fist trembled at his side, but he kept his eyes on the panel.
He answered quietly. 'I'm someone's relief.'
Beneath the table, amber pulsed in Taeo's palm. Nib let him feel his trembling fist through the link. The room went still. Bae ignored the red warning on his wrist and stayed.
Pyo removed his glasses. Mimicry could be very sophisticated, he said. Nib turned toward him and raised his open hand so everyone could see it shaking.
'Then why would I lie about being afraid?' Taeo started to rise, then stopped himself. Pyo studied Nib's hand. For a moment, something like doubt showed in his eyes.

After the recess, the panel denied Kanghan's petition. Nib was a registered arrival. A person. His status would remain pending for twelve months, renewable. It was enough for Taeo's relief to finally break through.
He laughed and cried at once. Nib offered him a napkin from his pouch, observing, 'You're leaking.' Nearby, Chae closed her eyes and let out a long breath.
Outside, her supervisor said the arrival report would still go in her staff review. Chae knew. Before leaving, he added that it had been a good report.
At registration, the clerk asked Nib to smile for his photograph. Nib refused. Taeo struggled to contain his laughter as the camera captured the scowl.
Nib slowly read his new card: registered arrival, person, with Yoon Taeo listed as his linked partner. Taeo was surprised he could read it. Nib admitted that he could, slowly.
With his knife returned, Nib relaxed. Pyo congratulated him on the photograph. Taeo handed back the business card Pyo had left at the café.
Pyo pocketed it without losing his patience. 'Pending isn't permanent, Mr. Yoon.' Then he walked away into the afternoon sun.
Chae caught them on the steps with a list of gates still open today. One Grade E gate in a subway maintenance tunnel had only an entrance photograph. Its full survey wasn't scheduled yet.
She had printed that photograph because Nib liked paper. He compared it with his drawing of the watch post. The white stone inside the gate looked like the white patch beside his wall.
Chae warned that the tunnel gate was still open, for now. Nib looked up at Taeo. He wanted to go in.
Grandpa's warning returned to Taeo. The fear was still there, even with tears from the hearing on his face. He told Nib he couldn't go in.
Nib held up his new ID card, steady and decided. 'I didn't ask you to.' Taeo stood caught between fear and something almost like relief.
